channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Layer-engineered quantum anomalous Hall effect in twisted rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Wei Zhu, Shuigang Xu

Authors: Zhangyuan Chen, Naitian Liu, Jiannan Hua, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Significant transport study on topological Chern phases and QAH in twisted graphene systems.

Tags: #graphene #quantumanomalousHall #topological

Abstract: Magnetotransport measurements on numerous samples of monolayer–multilayer (1 + N) rhombohedral graphene reveal a high-Chern-number quantum anomalous Hall effect with Chern number C = N. Further, in twisted Bernal bilayer–rhombohedral tetralayer graphene, a displacement-field-driven topological phase transition between C = 3 and C = 4 states is demonstrated.

item.title: [10] Goniopolar kagome materials boost transverse thermoelectricity
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 10/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct hit on kagome materials, flat bands, and van Hove singularities related to user projects.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #kagome #thermoelectricity #flatbands

Abstract: Thermoelectricity enables interconversion between heat and charge currents, but existing material platforms rely on constrained longitudinal geometries, complex fabrication or an external magnetic field to achieve high performance. Now, goniopolar kagome materials enable strong transversal thermoelectricity without an applied magnetic field, owing to flat electronic bands or van Hove singularities.

item.title: [9] Twisting light the Weyl way
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. Akrap, M. Orlita

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct relevance: magnetic topological materials (MnBi2Te4), Weyl physics, and circular dichroism.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #magnetictopologicalmaterial #Weyl #circulardichroism

Abstract: The application of a magnetic field to a Mn(Bi,Sb)2Te4 alloy induces concurrent magnetic and topological phase transitions, giving rise to unexpectedly strong circular dichroism in the infrared range.
